outcome: antenatal care characteristics (education, marital status, employment, disability, smoking, chronic concomitant diseases, antenatal visits, weight gain, hospitalization during pregnancy, postpartum hospitalization, breastfeeding)
cohort: The study included 131 pregnant women with pre-existing mental disorders matched to 228 mentally healthy controls, all of whom gave birth between 2006 and 2015 in a tertiary health care institution.
finding: Pregnant women with pre-existing mental health disorders experienced a worse course of pregnancy, including poorer antenatal care characteristics, and had an increased risk (RR 2.055) of delivering a small for gestational age newborn.
mod_finding: No difference was found between the groups when comparing methods of delivery.
